label: second input step when the first token was t
explanation: Fires at step 1 (the second original token) exactly when the first original token was t; it fires there every time (precision 1.0) at near-max magnitude (~3.0, about 0.96-1.0 of max), whatever the current token is. Magnitude barely varies; it is slightly higher (1.0 of max) when the current token is also t. A weak tail (about 0.01-0.1 of max, under 1% of mass) fires at step 2 in about 28% of cases where the step-1 token was t (e.g. m t [d]). It never fires at step 0, at steps 3 and later, or in the delimiter or copy phases, and it does not fire on t inputs themselves.

issues: The core claim holds. (t==1)&(prev_tok==t) has test precision 1.0, recall 0.782 and mass recall 0.991. The profile shows no firing at step 0, at step 3 or later, or in the delimiter or copy phases.

The tail is mischaracterized. It is not an unreliable 28% firing rate; it is deterministic once you know the FIRST token. Among steps where t==2 and the step-1 token was t, precision splits by first_tok: g, m, o, p, r, t, x give 1.0, k gives 0.9, u gives 0.56, and every other token gives 0.0. The 28% is just the average over first tokens. The dev precision of 0.64 that justified dropping the tail came from leaving out the first_tok condition.

Once that condition is added, the 'recall gap' disappears. The step-2 tail is all of the missing 22% of active steps (t==2 alone has recall 0.2177, the whole gap). By count it is a systematic class, even though it carries under 1% of the mass.
The label 'second input step when the first token was t' leaves out the step-2 firing, which is tied to an earlier token. By count, that is about 22% of all firings.
skeptic.revised_label: t as the most recent input in the first two steps: fires strongly (~3.0) at step 1 when orig(0)=t, and weakly (0.01-0.1 of max) at step 2 when orig(1)=t and orig(0) is in {g,k,m,o,p,r,t,x,u}
skeptic.better_predicate: ((t == 1) & (prev_tok == tok("t"))) | ((t == 2) & (prev_tok == tok('t')) & isin(first_tok, [tok(c) for c in ['g','k','m','o','p','r','t','x','u']]))
